content.overview: Article 59 provides the conditions of the President’s office: the President shall not be a member of either House of Parliament or of a House of the Legislature of any State (and if a member, is deemed to have vacated the seat on entering upon office as President); shall not hold any other office of profit; shall be entitled without payment of rent to the use of his official residences; and shall be entitled to such emoluments, allowances and privileges as Parliament may by law determine (and until so determined, as in the Second Schedule). Emoluments and allowances shall not be diminished during the term of office.
content.glance: Not a member of Parliament/State Legislature; no other office of profit; official residence; emoluments by law (not diminished during term).
content.study:
Article 59 conditions:
(1) Not a member of either House of Parliament or of a State Legislature; seat vacated on entering Presidential office if previously a member.
(2) Shall not hold any other office of profit.
(3) Entitled without payment of rent to use of official residences; emoluments, allowances and privileges as Parliament by law determines (interim: Second Schedule).
(4) Emoluments and allowances shall not be diminished during the term of office.

Examination: dual-membership ban; no office of profit; residence and emoluments; non-diminution during term.

sections.heading: Conditions
sections.body:
1. Not a member of Parliament or any State Legislature (seat vacated on entering office).
2. No other office of profit.
3. Official residences without rent; emoluments/allowances/privileges by parliamentary law.
4. Emoluments and allowances not to be diminished during the term.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What are the conditions of the President’s office under Article 59?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 59, the President shall not be a member of either House of Parliament or of a State Legislature, and shall not hold any other office of profit. He is entitled to official residences without payment of rent and to emoluments, allowances and privileges as determined by Parliament by law. Emoluments and allowances shall not be diminished during his term of office.

examTips: No dual membership; no office of profit; emoluments not diminished during term.

keyTakeaways: Art 59: conditions of President’s office; non-diminution of emoluments.
